lines: Quæ ſimul intonuit, proxima quæque fugat {e}.
Meſmes que de ceux, eſquels on peut colloquer quel
que fiance, ils ſ'en trouuent ſi difficillement, que le Phe-
nix quelquefois, n'eſt pas ſi rare: voire en ce temps, les
diſgraces en amitié ſont ſi grandes, que pluſieurs font
profeſsion auec nous d'intime amitié, & ſe monſtrent,
exterieurement pluſque noſtres, deſquels neantmoins l'e
prit & l'entendement eſt deſloyal: plein de de toute pro
dition, & de toutes parts noſtre aduerſaire: & ſous l'hon
neſte manteau d'amitié, ſont nos grans ennemis: plus
mauuais certes, & dangereux, que ceux qui pour tels
ouuertement ſe declarent {f}. Car quelle peſte pourroit
on ſonger plus violente, pernicieuſe, ni plus efficace à
nuire, qu'vn familier ennemy {g}, lequel nous à irrepara-
blemẽt offenſez, auant que ſe doubter de luy? ou toutes
fois, nous pouuons facilemẽt euiter celuy, qui ouuerte-
ment ſe monſtre noſtre aduerſaire {h}. Voila pourquoy:
faut bien eſtre prudent, à choiſir vn ami. & manger vn
muy de ſel auec vn homme: c'eſt à dire, conuerſer lon-
guement auec luy, auant qu'y mettre ſa fiance, & luy
commettre rien des choſes plus ſecrettes {i}. Traite ta cau
ſe (diſoit le Sage) auec ton ami, & ne reuele point tes
ſecrets à vn autre: que parauenture celuy qui t'eſcoute, ne
te le reproche, & que ce blaſme ne retourne ſur toy {k}. On
attribue encore à Bias, vne ſentẽce plus eſtroite, à ſçauoir
qu'il conuenoit tellement aimer vne perſonne, qu'on pen
ſaſt auſſi quelque iour le hayr {l}. ce que Publius Mimus
entre ſes plus graues ſentences, apres vſurpa, diſant.
Ita amicum habeas, poſſe vt fieri inimicũ putes.
Ayes ton ami en tel reng. que tu cuides qu'il peut à
l'aduenir eſtre ton ennemy. Paroles ainſi que Scipion eſ
crit aux œuures de Ciceron, les plus ennemis de l'ami-
tié qu'on pourrit excogiter: & ſi barbares, qu'il ne ſe pou
roit perſuader, que Bias, vn des ſept ſages, & tant renom-
mé les euſt vomies. Car comme eſt il poſſible, que tu
ſois vray ami de celuy, duquel tu crains, à l'aduenir eſtre
ſon ennemy {m}? Il eſt bien vray que comme il n'y a rien
de permanent en ce mõde {n}. l'amitié en tout temps & en
toutes perſonnes, ne peut pas eſtre perdurable, iuſqu'au

uncertain.text: Quæ ſimul intonuit, proxima quæque fugat {e}.
uncertain.note: the pentameter of the Ovid distich whose hexameter closes p009 ('Diligitur nemo...'), so continues_prev is true. At the far right, after the swash tail of the italic t, stand two small marks one above the other: the upper is read as the raised marker e (its note is printed beside this line), the lower as the closing point. The upper mark is tiny and could also be read as part of a colon.

uncertain.note: the apostrophe in 'iuſqu'au' is a small raised mark set tight between u and a; read as an apostrophe. The sentence continues on p011 (continues_next true).
two dotted minims before the point ('ij.'), checked at high magnification; not 'iij.'.
the numeral shows three dots over its minims (i, i, j), read 'xciij.'; the final two minims are set tight and a reader might count 'xcij.'. Tilde over the o of 'ſtinctiõ' is clear.
a point follows 'donatio', slightly below the baseline.

the first word is a compressed italic 'les' (l followed by a tight e-s group), not the clear 'la' of the g-note; could be read 'la'. Sense wants 'la iii.' (the third Verrine). Transcribed as it appears.

the key sort printed before 'Ariſtote' looks at high magnification like an 'a' with a grave accent ('à') rather than a plain italic i; the body marker (blocks[1].lines[19]) is clearly i, and the note occupies i's place in the sequence e-n, so it is keyed 'i'. Possibly a wrong sort for the key letter.
the key is the italic k whose stem and arms print as two separate strokes ('Ik'); same sort as the body marker after 'toy'. Read 'k'.

sic: the letters print L a c r e e ('Lacree'), transposed for 'Laerce' (Diogenes Laertius); checked at high magnification, the third letter is an open c and the fifth and sixth are e. Transcribed as printed.
sic for 'Priene'; transcribed as printed.
a tilde (flat bar) stands over the final a of 'Amici-|tiã', clear at high magnification; kept as printed though 'Amicitia' wants none.

a short grave-like stroke is printed above and to the left of the c of 'cũ', beside the tilde; read as stray ink or a displaced part of the tilde, not transcribed. 'deb ere' is set with a gap and normalized to 'debere'.
no point after 'C' in the print (contrast 'D.' and 'C.' in the g-note); transcribed without.
'predio' printed with plain e, not æ.
no foot citation block, no signature, no catchword; the lower third of the leaf below 'iuſqu'au' is blank.
